name: Mhondoro-Possessed Stone Giant
body:
MHONDORO-POSSESSED STONE GIANT
CR 9

XP 6,400
N Large humanoid (giant)
Init +2; Senses darkvision 120 ft., low-light vision; Perception +12

DEFENSE

AC 22, touch 11, flat-footed 20 (+2 Dex, +11 natural, –1 size)
hp 102 (12d8+48); regeneration 5 (electricity or fire)
Fort +14, Ref +8, Will +9
Defensive Abilities improved rock catching, unnatural vigor; Resist negative energy 5

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee greatclub +16/+11 (2d8+12) or 2 slams +16 (1d8+8)
Ranged rock +11/+6 (1d8+12)
Space 10 ft., Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks rock throwing (180 ft.)

STATISTICS

Str 27, Dex 15, Con 19, Int 10, Wis 12, Cha 10
Base Atk +9; CMB +18; CMD 30
Feats Iron Will, Martial Weapon Proficiency (greatclub), Point-Blank Shot, Power Attack, Precise Shot, Quick Draw
Skills Acrobatics +13 (+17 to jump), Climb +12, Intimidate +12, Knowledge (nobility) +4, Perception +12, Stealth +13 (+17 in rocky terrain); Racial Modifiers +8 Stealth in rocky terrain
Languages Common, Giant plus any two

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate mountains
Organization solitary
Treasure standard (greatclub, other treasure)

Lingering spirits of past kings, chiefs, and other great figures, mhondoro (also svikiro) inhabit maneless lions and lie in wait until they sense a host in need of their aid. When they sense such a creature, the mhondoro asks if that creature is willing to accept its aid, though it does not specify what form this aid will take. If the creature agrees, the mhondoro possesses it and aids the creature in its quest. How long a mhondoro inhabits its host varies based on the length and urgency of the host’s task. While most mhondoro are benevolent and attempt to honor the need of the creature they assist, some attempt to assert their will over the host. Even the most benevolent mhondoro exerts considerable influence over how the creature performs its quest—the “price” for its assistance.
